thread:
maria: Quick sync — trying to lock the sprint slice for the Optimize pilot. Customer asks (AcmeHealth) landed: adaptive batching + config hints, a simple quant fallback, and eval-triggered alerts. can we make a minimal acceptance checklist today?
chen: short answer: yes, but we need to trade p99 latency vs token cost. suggest 2 tracks: latency-sensitive (no aggressive batching, KV cache only) and cost-sensitive (aggressive batching + 8-bit quant).
oliver: +1. For pilot we should default to conservative quant fallback only on degradation signals, not global config. customers hate quality surprises.
sam: Can we define the eval-triggered alert rule as: "when eval set concordance drops >6% over 10k requests"? that gives noise control.
maria: that sounds reasonable. Also need rollout plan: canary to 5% customers, telemetry for prompt-level regression, auto-fallback to previous model variant.
chen: agree. Also get ops constraints: Resource-wise, dedicated GPU pools for canary required? if we use hosted slots, routing policies need a fallback. eng-bot: Deploy check triggered: canary-policy v2 needs a rollout flag.
oliver: acceptance checklist proposal: 1) Policy DSL for batching/caching exposed in console (simple toggles + advanced yaml). 2) Quant fallback path implemented + smoke tests. 3) Eval-alert pipeline wired to SLOs & slack ops channel. 4) Canary rollout automation + rollback hook.
maria: adding minimum perf gates: end-to-end p50 <= 120ms for latency track, p99 <= 450ms, and cost track should show >15% token-cost reduction in internal bench.
sam: For eval-trigger rules, also add manual mute and rate limit for alerts. ops gets a weekly digest and urgent alerts to #eng-oncall.
chen: small engineering note: batching heuristic needs a cheap estimator for token distribution to pick batch window. start with moving-average seq length over 1k requests. code hint: ```yaml batching_policy: window_ms: auto_min: 5 max: 50 estimator: moving_avg_seq```
maria: customers asked for a brief UX: one-click "Apply recommendations" for quant/batching with preview of estimated $$ saved + p99 impact. we should add that to MVP scope if it doesn't blow the sprint.
oliver: UX could be minimal: a modal with 3 bullets + estimated savings. engineering can wire placeholder numbers initially.
chen: timeline: 2-week sprint for core engine + eval-alert plumbing, 1-week follow-up for console and canary automation. Is that realistic?
maria: ok lock that as target. if we hit blocker on batching estimator, fallback to static presets (mobile, desktop, high-throughput).
sam: I'm happy to own the eval signal thresholds and dashboard. i'll produce a short spec doc and example alerts.
maria: perfect. action items: @chen prototype estimator, @oliver quant fallback smoke, @sam eval-alert spec, @maria coordinate canary plan with ops. I'll schedule a 30m demo on Thu. :thumbsup:
